name: Change at a ticket kiosk
brief:
A museum kiosk sells £5 tickets and opens with an empty till. Customers queue in the order of `notes`; each pays for one ticket with a single £5, £10 or £20 note and must get exact change. Change is given only in £5 and £10 notes, since £20 notes go straight into the safe.

Write `first_short_change(notes)`, which returns the position (from 0) of the first customer the kiosk cannot give change to, or -1 if everyone is served.

Example. For `[5, 5, 10, 20, 20]` the till holds two £5 notes, then one £5 and one £10. The first £20 takes both, so the second £20 at position 4 cannot be changed. The answer is 4.
constraints: $O(n)$ time is the target. Recounting the till from the start for each customer is too slow.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Keep counts of £5 and £10 notes. For £15 change, give a £10 and a £5 when you can, and three £5 notes only when you must.

examples.note: The first £20 uses the last £10 and £5, leaving nothing for the second.
Giving £10 and £5 for the £20 keeps a £5 spare; everyone is served.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Greedy choice with its proof: for a £20, give £10 and £5 when possible. Against three £5 notes, that keeps two more £5 notes and one fewer £10, and two £5 notes can always do a £10's job.
A £10 note needs a £5 back, so the very first £10 with an empty till fails; three £5 notes are the fallback only when no £10 is in the till.
One pass with two counters is $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ memory.
